peaq:
About peaq

Somewhere on robotic.sh right now, a robot is renting GPU time it doesn't own. Another is buying a centimeter-accurate position fix. A vertical farm in Hong Kong that was tokenized on Dualmint is paying revenue from salad sales to the people who co-own it. No purchase order, no invoice, no human in the loop. That is the Machine Economy, and it is already running. DePINs all over the world are aggregating training data, providing compute and storage for machines, and building an entire infrastructure layer for robots and machines to run on.

peaq is the omnichain economic system enabling robots and machines to do business on every chain. Machines earn, transact, build a credit rating, access capital, and become investable assets — economic participants, not endpoints owned by somebody else. We've got over 6M robots, machines, and humans onboarded, with 60+ apps across 22 industries, and 48M+ transactions settled by machines. We're excited to see what you build for the Machine Economy at the Crypto World's Fair!

Mission

Build something that advances the Machine Economy. We're looking for innovative solutions that empower physical hardware or offer services like credit, coordination, ownership, or income generation for machines.

Hackathon Track Scope

We're looking for projects that push the boundaries of the Machine Economy. Your project could fall into one of these areas, or something entirely new:

Robotics: Give robots an onchain identity, a wallet, and the ability to earn and pay for themselves.

Machine-to-machine commerce: Enable machines to pay each other for data, energy, compute, or work without human intervention.

Physical AI: Develop agents that can operate, coordinate, or transact on behalf of real hardware.

DeFi for Machines: Explore tokenization, fractional ownership, revenue sharing, lending, credit, or insurance specifically for machines.

DePINs: Focus on energy, mobility, compute, connectivity, or sensing applications within decentralized physical infrastructure networks.

You don't necessarily need physical hardware for your submission. A simulated machine that activates a real machine ID and reports real revenue or activity events is a valid submission.

Here are some starter ideas, but feel free to think outside the box:

Credit in motion: Activate a machine, stream its revenue events, and build a dashboard that shows its Machine Credit Rating increasing in real-time. This proves end-to-end activation and qualification.

New robotic.sh adapter: Create something valuable that machines would pay for, something not already among the existing 20 adapters. Ship the adapter and demonstrate one machine calling it to prove the service layer is open.

Two machines, one deal: Show a drone paying a charging pad, or a car paying a parking sensor, with the transaction settled onchain without human approval. This proves M2M settlement.

Parametric insurance: Write a downtime policy where the machine's own signed telemetry acts as the trigger. If heartbeats stop, escrow pays out without a claims adjuster. Price the premium based on its credit rating. This demonstrates how verifiable telemetry makes a machine insurable.

Secondary market for machines: Build a listing and settlement mechanism for a Machine NFT (the tradeable kind, not the soulbound Identity NFT). Render the listing like a bond, showing live ratings, trailing revenue, and implied yield. This proves machines can trade based on cashflow.

We welcome early-stage and unfinished-but-promising work. We're more interested in a strong idea with a clear direction than a finished product without a compelling vision.

What won't score well:

An excellent app with peaq tacked on as an afterthought.

Another generic fleet dashboard that lacks an underlying economic mechanism.

A pitch deck and roadmap instead of a working demo.

A README that assumes we already understand your project.

Five partially built features instead of one fully functional one.

Submission Requirements

Your submission should be a working demo or a compelling prototype.

Clearly articulate how your project contributes to the Machine Economy.

Provide a clear explanation of your project's functionality and purpose.

Submissions must be in English.

Judging Criteria

Submissions will be judged on:

Innovation and Creativity: How novel and imaginative is your solution for advancing the Machine Economy?

Technical Implementation: The quality of your code, the feasibility of your solution, and how well it integrates with peaq's principles (even if simulated).

Impact and Potential: How significantly could your project move the Machine Economy forward, and what is its potential for real-world application?

Clarity and Presentation: How well you explain your idea, its functionality, and its value.

Adherence to the Machine Economy Focus: Projects that genuinely address the challenges and opportunities within the Machine Economy, rather than simply incorporating peaq without clear economic mechanisms.

Reward Structure

1st Place: 1000 USDT + 1 Microducks + an introduction to the peaq ecosystem and BD team, and a participation in peaq’s and codec’s Foundry Program

2nd Place: 700 USDT + 1 Microduck (worth 399USD)*

3rd Place: 300 USDT + 1 Microduck (worth 399USD)*

4th Place: 1 Microduck (worth 399USD)* - This is not a cash price

5th Place: 1 Microduck (worth 399USD)* - This is not a cash price 
*Please note: due to high demand, there may be delays in Microduck delivery. This is outside of peaq's control and we appreciate your patience.

solami:
About the Bounty
Solami is Solana infrastructure for builders and traders: private RPC, the Yellowstone gRPC firehose, decoded market data, webhooks and transaction landing, all behind one API key and all on our own bare metal. Teams come to us when public endpoints stop being good enough, and pay for what they actually use, billed by the byte or the request.

What to Build
Build something that runs on Solana in real time: a trading bot, an indexer, an alert system, a dashboard, a dev tool, an SDK. Read the chain through our APIs, act on it through Beam if it sends as well as reads, run it against mainnet, and open source it. We point new developers at the best submissions and feature the standouts across our channels.

The stack you have access to
Use whichever pieces fit:
- RPC: the RPC you already know, plus WebSocket subscriptions
- Yellowstone gRPC: the firehose. Accounts, transactions, slots, blocks and entries the moment they land, filtered server-side so you only pull what you asked for, with slot replay to close the gap after a reconnect
- Mirage: the same Yellowstone data over a plain WebSocket if you would rather not run a gRPC client
- Blur: decoded market data. Trades, token launches, liquidity changes, new pools and candles across every major DEX, over REST or WebSocket, with no instruction parsing on your side
- Data API (api.solami.dev): balances, history and indexed lookups
- Webhooks: push events to your endpoint instead of holding a connection
- Beam: transaction landing, for anything that sends rather than reads

Metrics to Include
Surface whatever your build actually answers, whether that is 24h volume and trade counts, unique wallets, new token launches and pool creations, liquidity moving in and out, per-token price, holders and buy versus sell pressure, or stream and transaction landing health.

Submission Requirements
1. Solami is the data path. At least one of the products above doing real work, not a token call.
2. Public repo with a README anyone can run: setup, env vars, how to point it at their own key.
3. A short demo, 2 to 3 minutes, video or Loom, running against live mainnet.
4. It works. A submission that does not run live is not judged.




Judging Criteria
1. Solami Usage: Uses Solami meaningfully as part of the build, not just a basic API call.
2. Working Demo: Runs live on Solana mainnet and clearly shows the product actually works.
3. Build Quality: Clean, reliable, and easy for others to understand and run.
4. Usefulness: Solves a real problem for traders, builders, or Solana users.
5. Creativity: Does something interesting with Solami or combines its tools in a unique way.

Getting a key
Sign up with this link and you get Pro free for 7 days: https://solami.dev/signup?ref=st-earn-sep-26

Pro covers everything in this bounty: 2 unmetered gRPC streams, 1 TB of Blur data, and 200 requests per second on RPC.

About CertiK

CertiK is a pioneer in blockchain security, utilizing best-in-class AI technology to secure and monitor blockchain projects. We're an innovator in the blockchain security space, combining academic expertise with enterprise-grade solutions to protect the web3 world. For the Crypto World's Fair hackathon, we're excited to support builders by providing essential security resources.

Mission

Our goal is to back promising projects emerging from the Crypto World's Fair hackathon by providing critical security audits, helping them launch confidently on mainnet, and attracting further investment.

Hackathon Track Scope

This track is for any team submitting a project to the Crypto World's Fair hackathon that plans to launch on mainnet and raise capital post-hackathon. We're looking for projects building for the long run, especially those handling user funds or on-chain value (DeFi, payments, stablecoins, RWAs, consumer apps with real assets). If you want to show investors and users that security is a core part of your foundation from day one, this track is for you.

Submission Requirements

To enter, tell us about your project and its future plans. Your submission should include:

Your Colosseum hackathon submission link and a public GitHub repo (or access instructions).

A brief description of your project, the problem it solves, and your target users.

Details on the programs/contracts you want audited, including approximate line count, and your target mainnet launch date.

Your 6–12 month roadmap, covering planned product releases, integrations, and key milestones (like token launches, new markets, or institutional partnerships).

Your team's details: names, roles, X/GitHub handles, and whether the core team is working full-time on the project.

Your fundraising status and plans: whether you're bootstrapped, grant-funded, have already raised, or are currently raising—including target round, timing, and any focus on regulated markets or institutional partners.

The best contact for a scoping call (Telegram handle or email).

Judging Criteria

Winners will be selected based on:

Security Relevance: The value at risk and amount of funds handled by the project.

Technical Maturity: How feature-complete or testnet-ready your code is.

Fundability and Long-Term Commitment: A credible roadmap, a dedicated team, and a clear path from hackathon to a funded, live product.

Codebase Quality: The clarity and overall quality of your project's code.

Overall Project Quality and Originality: The innovation and execution of your project.

About RPC Fast

RPC Fast provides high-performance Solana mainnet RPC and data streaming infrastructure, from lightweight endpoints for early-stage development to production-grade infrastructure.

We offer teams access to high-performance infrastructure throughout the hackathon and the post-hackathon evaluation period.

Hackathon Track Scope

All Colosseum participants can claim free access to the Focus plan for up to two months. Other plans are available upon request based on the project fit.

Keep building after the hackathon and share your journey with the Solana ecosystem. The strongest teams with the most engagement will be rewarded with 1-2 months of low latency RPC and gRPC infrastructure access.

Note: RPC Fast currently provides mainnet endpoints only, with infrastructure hosted in Frankfurt (FRA).

Offer period: September 15 – November 15. This timeline is for RPC access, not for track submissions. Submissions close on the specified deadline.

Eligibility

Submit your project to both the Colosseum hackathon and RPC Fast Superteam Infrastructure Sidetrack.

Your project must be eligible as per the official rules of the global hackathon.

Use RPC Fast infrastructure during and after the hackathon. Fill out the application form to claim the Focus plan access for up to two months (other plans are available upon request, based on the project profile).

Follow @rpcfast on X.

Join our Telegram and Discord communities for support and updates.

Publish at least 2–3 posts per month about RPC Fast in the next two months. Share your experience, progress, use case, or feedback.

Bonus engagement

Additional interaction is welcome and will be considered when selecting the winners:

Quotes and reposts of RPC Fast posts; replies and comments.

Educational or technical content featuring your build.

Community interaction across RPC Fast's X, Telegram, and Discord channels.

Judging Criteria

Project: concept, originality, and execution.

Infrastructure use: meaningful use of RPC Fast.

Community presence: consistency and quality of engagement.

Impact: overall visibility and value generated for the RPC Fast community.

The goal is to reward teams that build great products, use the infrastructure meaningfully, and actively share their journey with the community.

Ready to build? Let's support each other.

Reward Structure

Total reward pool: ~$10,500 in RPC infrastructure credits distributed across 21 selected teams. Each team is eligible for an equivalent of ~$500 prize.

Each selected team receives one of the following infrastructure packages, based on their choice:

One month of the Aperture subscription – $499 value. Best for high-load and trading apps. Access to Shredstream gRPC and our optimised TxStream gRPC (decoded shreds stream) with ALT resolution and optional real-time transaction simulation.

Two months of the Stream subscription – $498 value. Ideal for data-intensive apps with less extensive compute usage and mostly relying on Yellowstone gRPC usage.

Build faster. Keep your infrastructure running
Terms & Conditions

Infrastructure usage and acceptable activity
RPC Fast reserves the right to suspend or terminate access to any plan, including prize subscriptions, in cases of abuse, prohibited activity, excessive or unreasonable load, spam, or any other activity that violates RPC Fast's Terms of Service, or materially affects the service or other customers. 

Prize value
The prize value is limited to $499 (1 month of Aperture plan usage) or $498 (if two months of Stream plan selected) equivalent.

Form of rewards
All prizes are provided exclusively in the form of RPC Fast subscription plans assigned to the selected teams. Prizes are not paid or transferred as cash, cryptocurrency, or other monetary funds.

Prize activation
Prize subscriptions will be assigned to selected teams within two (2) weeks after the official announcement of the sidetrack results. The subscription will be scheduled to start immediately upon assignment. 

No rescheduling or cash equivalent
It is the participant's responsibility to use the awarded subscription during its assigned period. Unused subscription time, CU credits, or other included resources cannot be carried over, rescheduled, extended, or exchanged for cash, cryptocurrency, or any other monetary equivalent.

Plan selection
Winning teams may choose between the Aperture and Stream plans, subject to infrastructure fit and the team choice. RPC Fast may recommend the most appropriate plan based on the project's supported network, infrastructure requirements, and expected load, while remaining within the applicable prize limits.

Feel free to contact us on Telegram if you have any questions.
